column3: First formula witness: iman and salihat are joined to an enduring outcome.
Immediate context gives disciplined worship, sincerity, prayer, and zakat as the commanded practice.
Uses khayr for an inward responsiveness that would receive hearing rather than turn away.
Reprises the formula while adding humble return to the Lord; outcome is otherwise already covered.
Immediate context locates the bayyinah in a messenger reciting purified pages.
Directly ties iman and excellent work to preservation of recompense; supports f01 and f05.
Adds forgiveness and generous provision to recompense for the formula group.
Paired contrary verdict supplies the negative pole to 98:7's creature-ranking.
Contrary case: denial empties works of weight, clarifying that work is not self-validating.
Adds capacity as a limit on obligation alongside iman, salihat, and the enduring outcome.
Completes the immediate description of the upright contents of the purified pages.
Keeps righteous and lesser paths differentiated; its contrast route remains a boundary, not support.
Connects the formula to prayer, zakat, recompense, and freedom from fear and grief.
Immediate prelude frames refusal as persisting until the bayyinah arrives.
A temporal khayr comparison offers only a remote comparative parallel.
Challenges any claim that disbelievers possess comparative superiority; useful f03 boundary.
Immediate sequel specifies recompense, mutual approval, and reverent fear for the 98:7 group.
Shows khayr operating as a comparison of worth; retained contrast is boundary evidence.
Addresses believers with a concrete priority over trade and names that choice khayr.
Immediate contrast: division follows the arrival of the bayyinah.
Repentance joined to repair gives a remedial form of f02's righteous action.
Sets fire against secure arrival and makes deeds visible to divine sight; a moral-polarity boundary.
Adds forgiveness, gardens, and reward for workers, though the outcome pattern is now familiar.
Links wrongdoing, repentance, and a better course before the Creator.
Uses khayr in a narrow portrayal of withholding; little connects it to 98:7's criterion.
Presents repentance as the better response within an explicit refusal alternative.
Pairs repentance with repair after wrongdoing, extending the restorative side of f02.
Separates each party's works and responsibility; supports accountable action without equating outcomes.
Negative boundary: a settled word is followed by non-belief, highlighting the response dimension.
Another formula-to-gardens instance, substantially redundant with earlier cards.
States flourishing for believers; it supports the positive valuation but leaves action implicit.
Unending recompense for the formula group is a largely redundant outcome witness.
Gives believers a concrete integrity test through prohibition of betrayal and breach of trusts.
Adds bestowed affection as a social consequence of iman and salihat.
Links a peace-abode to what its people were doing, reinforcing action's relevance to outcome.
Formula plus good return repeats already established outcome evidence.
Places believer and disbeliever within one created field while deeds remain seen; useful for f03.
Admission among the righteous adds a group-placement dimension to salihat.
Work here concerns a distinct narrative service and does not clarify the 98:7 criterion.
Formula-to-gardens repetition adds little after multiple earlier witnesses.
Makes people encounter their works, directly strengthening f05's attributable-action dimension.
Adds removal of evil and recompense according to the best of deeds.
Creation language is too general to explain creature-ranking or iman with salihat.
Another formula-and-gardens witness, now redundant despite its retained routes.
Tests striving and exclusive alliance, but only indirectly bears on the focus formula.
Promise of forgiveness and great reward repeats the established formula outcome.
Faith with salihat is associated with the highest degrees, sharpening graded positive status.
Presents belief and taqwa as yielding a better divine return; adjacent but not identical to the focus.
Contrary boundary: lack of iman is joined to annulled works and miserliness toward khayr.
Payment of wages for the formula group is redundant recompense evidence.
A pressured claim of iman is too limited to establish the focus's durable pairing.
Repeated iman, taqwa, and ihsan add a layered ethical discipline to righteous action.
Treats signs as addressed to believers, supporting the evidence-and-response side of f01.
Adds patience to salihat before forgiveness and great reward.
Its rejected comparative route concerns a scene of fruit, not the focus criterion.
Imaan guides the formula group, adding a process between trust, action, and outcome.
Its question after discourse frames belief as a response to received speech; contrast remains boundary evidence.
Formula-to-gardens wording is redundant with earlier outcome cards.
Extends faith, last-day orientation, and righteous work across named communities without fear or grief.
Connects Quranic guidance, uprightness, believing workers, and a great reward.
Withholds judgment about others' works; only a limited accountability boundary.
Links iman and salihat to collective security, establishment, and exclusive worship.
Associates a hasanah with something better and security, a secondary benefit-oriented parallel.
Rejects equal treatment of evil-doers and the iman-salihat group; strong f03 polarity evidence.
Names worship and taqwa as the better course, a nearby choice-based parallel.
Identifies the focus-type group as heirs but supplies no criterion in this isolated verse.
Contrary boundary: association can annul work, qualifying f05's action-to-outcome relation.
Joins glad tidings for the formula group with increase in hasanah and gratitude.
Historical selection language only loosely parallels 98:7's status claim.
Contrasts full reward and added favor for the formula group with punishment for arrogant refusal.
Divine creation and observation of deeds are too general here to add a focus-specific link.
Situates iman and salihat against mutual injustice, with their scarcity noted in a social dispute.
Message-rejection language is only a distant response-to-belief parallel; reject route is boundary evidence.
Sets the formula group's gardens against a contrary unbelieving condition, but repeats the outcome pattern.
Connects worship, zakat, and advancing khayr with finding a greater recompense.
Another formula-and-eternal-gardens instance, redundant after earlier coverage.
Witnessing harm to believers does not materially explain their status or righteous work.
Return, equitable recompense for iman and salihat, and a contrary refusal outcome form a full polarity frame.
Extends iman and salihat with mutual commitment to truth and patience; strong social f02 evidence.
Unqualified promise of eternal gardens is redundant formula-outcome evidence.
Wisdom called abundant khayr is a remote benefit parallel, not the focus's ranking.
Makes iman with salihat open to men and women alike, with explicit non-injustice.
Belief versus turning away supplies only a thin, context-bound response contrast.
Ornamented gardens add descriptive reward detail but no new criterion.
Projected future righteousness after grave wrongdoing is a cautionary, not explanatory, use of salihat.
Early formula-and-gardens wording is redundant with stronger outcome witnesses already reviewed.
Grief over refusal of the discourse supports the seriousness of the belief-response boundary.
Parallel multi-community formula now substantially duplicates 5:69.
Pairs iman and righteous action with the best recompense and eased command.
Garden description and eternity are redundant outcome material.
Expands birr into belief, giving, worship, covenant fidelity, and endurance; rich f02 evidence.
Direct contrary: corruption is defined by failure to repair, sharply delimiting f02.
Measured provision alone does not clarify iman, salihat, or comparative creature-status.
Signs for believers provide only a general evidence-response parallel.
The assertion of manifest ingratitude has no sufficiently specific route to the focus.
A messenger's trustworthiness is only an indirect background to receiving a message.
Evidence and knowledge do not compel compliance when desires are followed; useful refusal boundary.
Commands just reconciliation between fighting believers, a concrete and strong f02 realization.
The isolated statement provides no usable connection to the focus.
Rejection based on followers' low social standing is a contrary social-status boundary for f01.
Connects iman, migration, striving, and divine non-loss of any worker's deed.
States non-injustice and multiplication of a hasanah, directly sharpening f05.
Links obedience to God and the messenger with exemplary companion placement.
Differentiates degrees through striving, a clear status-by-action parallel.
Extends the degree distinction with forgiveness and mercy.
Commands competition in khayrat; a direct action-oriented comparative frame.
Links truthful speech and recompense, a secondary accountability witness.
Joins truthfulness, gardens, and mutual approval; closely parallels 98:8.
Assigns degrees according to deeds, directly supporting non-arbitrary ranking.
Sets a multiplied hasanah against an unmultiplied sayyi'ah; strong f05 polarity.
Makes the weight of scales decisive, reinforcing the evaluative dimension of deeds.
Links garden inheritance to deeds while portraying removal of rancor.
Names iman, migration, and striving as grounds for greater degree and success.
Pairs gardens with divine pleasure, a close complement to 98:8.
Presents divine approval and gardens for a defined believing community.
Combines patience, worship, giving, and repelling evil with the good final abode.
Contrasts those who do ihsan with the deniers and calls the later abode better.
Joins iman and salih action to good life and best-form recompense without sex distinction.
Makes believing pursuit and striving the condition for accepted endeavor.
Pairs iman and salihat with an enduring good recompense in the Qur'anic message frame.
Joins hope of meeting the Lord, salih action, and rejection of association.
Links repentance, iman, and salih action to garden entry.
Associates purification with eternal gardens and the best outcome.
Affirms that a believer's salih striving is not lost; direct f05 support.
Begins a clustered portrait of those reverently aware of their Lord.
Describes the preceding believing group as hastening toward khayrat.
Makes heavy scales the marker of success, a direct evaluation parallel.
Joins repentance, iman, and salih action with transformation of sayyi'at into hasanat.
Links patient endurance and repelling evil with doubled reward.
Gives the formula group an abiding garden dwelling, though outcome material is familiar.
Places iman and salihat in a garden of rejoicing.
Contrasts the formula group with fasiqun through distinct abodes.
Provides a broad paired inventory of faithful virtues and forgiveness with great reward.
Contrasts denial's punishment with forgiveness and great reward for iman and salihat.
Links recitation, prayer, spending, and hoped-for divine return.
Connects ihsan with good and gives patience an unmeasured reward.
Treats bringing and confirming truth as the mark of taqwa.
Sets sayyi'ah's like-for-like return against unbounded provision for believing salih action.
States that salih action returns to oneself and evil action likewise.
Brings believers and their spouses into the garden with joy.
Joins declaration of the Lord with steadfastness and freedom from fear and grief.
Gives the steadfast group abiding garden recompense for deeds.
Joins iman, salihat, and belief in the revealed message with expiation and rectification.
Combines faith, communal discipline, and promise of forgiveness and great reward.
Places honor among created peoples on taqwa, a major boundary for f03's superiority claim.
Uses a good loan and multiplied recompense, a secondary f04 and f05 parallel.
Joins belief in God and messengers with truthfulness, reward, and light.
Explicitly raises believers and those given knowledge in degrees.
Frames iman and striving as a saving exchange, adding purposeful action.
Gives forgiveness and gardens as the stated outcome of the preceding iman and striving.
Joins iman and salih action with expiation and gardens; a concise later formula witness.
Links taqwa to expiation of sayyi'at and magnified reward.
Calls for sincere repentance and describes expiation and garden entry.
Makes life and death a test of which person is best in deed; central f03 and f05 evidence.
States that every self is held to what it has earned, supporting attributable action.
Identifies a recompense as reward for prior striving.
Gives iman and salihat an unbroken reward, though it is outcome-redundant.
Repeats the iman-salihat exception with an unbroken reward.
Makes even an atom-weight of khayr visible, an essential f05 action-accountability witness.
Supplies the corresponding visible sayyi'ah boundary for 99:7.
